label: Spatial granularity
description: Ability to divide inhabitants into smaller social/spatial units rather than one large undifferentiated population.
phrase: the architecture's ability to divide people into smaller units

label: Sensory compartmentalization
description: Ability to keep sound, odor, moisture, light, conflict, and activity in one area from propagating throughout the environment.
phrase: the containment of sound, light, odor, and activity within areas

label: Wet-core / plumbing design
description: Adequacy, separation, drainage, ventilation, durability, and capacity of toilets, sinks, and showers.

label: Daylight & exterior orientation
description: Access to natural light, visible day/night cues, sky, horizon, or other exterior temporal information.

label: Exterior permeability
description: Practical access to outdoor air, sun, weather, recreation, and an environment beyond the enclosed interior.

label: Acoustic refuge
description: Availability of spaces in which a person can escape or substantially reduce communal, mechanical, television, intercom, and impact noise.
phrase: the availability of quieter refuge space

label: Functional adjacency
description: Whether sleeping, sanitation, dining, medical, legal, recreation, and other functions are appropriately separated yet practically reachable.
phrase: the arrangement of functions — separated yet reachable

label: Circulation autonomy
description: Degree to which a person can move among permitted spaces without every transition requiring staff intervention, escort, search, or door release.
phrase: the ability to move among permitted spaces without staff mediation

label: Climate envelope / HVAC resilience
description: Ability to maintain tolerable temperature, ventilation, humidity, and air quality as occupancy and weather change.

label: Horizontal space & sleep infrastructure
description: Ability to provide each person with a stable place to lie down, sleep, store basic belongings, and remain out of circulation paths.
phrase: the provision of a stable place to lie down

label: Territorial connectivity
description: Architectural/logistical connection to hospitals, courts, lawyers, family visitation, transport, and other external services.
phrase: the site's connection to outside services

label: Inspectability / observational permeability
description: Ability of independent inspectors, attorneys, family, monitors, and other legitimate outsiders to observe conditions and communicate privately with inhabitants.
phrase: the ability of legitimate outsiders to observe and communicate

label: Spatial differentiation
description: Availability of genuinely different environments during the day: sleep space, dining space, outdoor space, medical space, legal space, recreation space, quiet space, etc.
phrase: the availability of genuinely different environments
